newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks close flat, watch for labor deal.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks close flat, watch for labor deal.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed broadly flat in slow trade, hemmed in by a temporary liquidity squeeze and investors who waited out the day for more details of the severance pay reform deal reached last weekend.
Brokers said trade had been stifled by overnight bank rates that rose to 70 percent from 50 percent on Friday.
"The market was also watching for President Rafael Caldera's formal announcement this evening about severance pay reform," said Multinvest broker Jose Gregorio Tineo.

Government, union and private sector leaders reached agreement on crucial reform of Venezuela's onerous severance pay system early Saturday. The reforms are expected to free up labor markets, paving the way for a long awaited restructuring of Venezuela's bloated public sector.
The 19-share index closed marginally off at 6,384.03 points, down 0.11 percent, as 19 million shares traded worth 3.8 billion bolivars ($7.9 million).
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, closed down 0.27 percent at 98.60.

CANTV, which surged late last week on news second quarter tariff increases had been approved, slipped 10.00 bolivars to close at 2100.00 despite a buy recommendation from investment house HSBC James Capel.
Among other traded stocks, 20 rose, 15 fell and seven closed flat.
